description: This module allows the administration of Keycloak clients using the Keycloak REST API. It requires access to the REST API using OpenID Connect; the user connecting and the client being used must have the requisite access rights. In a default Keycloak installation, admin-cli and an admin user would work, as would a separate client definition with the scope tailored to your needs and a user having the expected roles.

parameters.name: admin_url
parameters.description: URL to the admin interface of the client. This is adminUrl in the Keycloak REST API.

parameters.name: always_display_in_console
parameters.description: Whether or not to display this client in account console, even if the user does not have an active session. Choices: false true

parameters.name: attributes
parameters.description: A dict of further attributes for this client. This can contain various configuration settings; an example is given in the examples section. While an exhaustive list of permissible options is not available; possible options as of Keycloak 3.4 are listed below. The Keycloak API does not validate whether a given option is appropriate for the protocol used; if specified anyway, Keycloak does not use it.

parameters.name: jwks.url
parameters.description: For OpenID-Connect clients, URL where client keys in JWK are stored.

parameters.name: jwt.credential.certificate
parameters.description: For OpenID-Connect clients, client certificate for validating JWT issued by client and signed by its key, base64-encoded.

parameters.name: request.object.signature.alg
parameters.description: For OpenID-Connect clients, JWA algorithm which the client needs to use when sending OIDC request object. One of any, none, RS256.

parameters.name: saml.authnstatement
parameters.description: For SAML clients, boolean specifying whether or not a statement containing method and timestamp should be included in the login response.

parameters.name: saml.client.signature
parameters.description: For SAML clients, boolean specifying whether a client signature is required and validated.

parameters.name: saml.encrypt
parameters.description: Boolean specifying whether SAML assertions should be encrypted with the client’s public key.

parameters.name: saml.force.post.binding
parameters.description: For SAML clients, boolean specifying whether always to use POST binding for responses.

parameters.name: saml.onetimeuse.condition
parameters.description: For SAML clients, boolean specifying whether a OneTimeUse condition should be included in login responses.

parameters.name: saml.server.signature
parameters.description: Boolean specifying whether SAML documents should be signed by the realm.

parameters.name: saml.server.signature.keyinfo.ext
parameters.description: For SAML clients, boolean specifying whether REDIRECT signing key lookup should be optimized through inclusion of the signing key ID in the SAML Extensions element.

parameters.name: saml.signature.algorithm
parameters.description: Signature algorithm used to sign SAML documents. One of RSA_SHA256, RSA_SHA1, RSA_SHA512, or DSA_SHA1.

parameters.name: saml.signing.certificate
parameters.description: SAML signing key certificate, base64-encoded.

parameters.name: saml.signing.private.key
parameters.description: SAML signing key private key, base64-encoded.

parameters.name: saml_assertion_consumer_url_post
parameters.description: SAML POST Binding URL for the client’s assertion consumer service (login responses).

parameters.name: saml_assertion_consumer_url_redirect
parameters.description: SAML Redirect Binding URL for the client’s assertion consumer service (login responses).

parameters.name: saml_force_name_id_format
parameters.description: For SAML clients, Boolean specifying whether to ignore requested NameID subject format and using the configured one instead.

parameters.name: saml_name_id_format
parameters.description: For SAML clients, the NameID format to use (one of username, email, transient, or persistent).

parameters.name: saml_signature_canonicalization_method
parameters.description: SAML signature canonicalization method. This is one of four values, namely http://www.w3.org/2001/10/xml-exc-c14n# for EXCLUSIVE, http://www.w3.org/2001/10/xml-exc-c14n#WithComments for EXCLUSIVE_WITH_COMMENTS, http://www.w3.org/TR/2001/REC-xml-c14n-20010315 for INCLUSIVE, and http://www.w3.org/TR/2001/REC-xml-c14n-20010315#WithComments for INCLUSIVE_WITH_COMMENTS.

parameters.name: saml_single_logout_service_url_post
parameters.description: SAML POST binding URL for the client’s single logout service.

parameters.name: saml_single_logout_service_url_redirect
parameters.description: SAML redirect binding URL for the client’s single logout service.

parameters.name: use.jwks.url
parameters.description: For OpenID-Connect clients, boolean specifying whether to use a JWKS URL to obtain client public keys.

parameters.name: user.info.response.signature.alg
parameters.description: For OpenID-Connect clients, JWA algorithm for signed UserInfo-endpoint responses. One of RS256 or unsigned.

parameters.name: x509.allow.regex.pattern.comparison
parameters.description: For OpenID-Connect clients, boolean specifying whether to allow x509.subjectdn as regular expression. Choices: false true

parameters.name: x509.subjectdn
parameters.description: For OpenID-Connect clients, subject which is used to authenticate the client.

parameters.name: auth_client_id
parameters.description: OpenID Connect client_id to authenticate to the API with. Default: "admin-cli"

parameters.name: auth_client_secret
parameters.description: Client Secret to use in conjunction with auth_client_id (if required).

parameters.name: auth_keycloak_url
parameters.description: URL to the Keycloak instance.

parameters.name: auth_password
parameters.description: Password to authenticate for API access with.

parameters.name: auth_realm
parameters.description: Keycloak realm name to authenticate to for API access.

parameters.name: auth_username
parameters.description: Username to authenticate for API access with.

parameters.name: authentication_flow_binding_overrides
parameters.description: Override realm authentication flow bindings.

parameters.name: browser
parameters.description: Flow ID of the browser authentication flow. authentication_flow_binding_overrides.browser and authentication_flow_binding_overrides.browser_name are mutually exclusive.

parameters.name: browser_name
parameters.description: Flow name of the browser authentication flow. authentication_flow_binding_overrides.browser and authentication_flow_binding_overrides.browser_name are mutually exclusive.

parameters.name: direct_grant
parameters.description: Flow ID of the direct grant authentication flow. authentication_flow_binding_overrides.direct_grant and authentication_flow_binding_overrides.direct_grant_name are mutually exclusive.

parameters.name: direct_grant_name
parameters.description: Flow name of the direct grant authentication flow. authentication_flow_binding_overrides.direct_grant and authentication_flow_binding_overrides.direct_grant_name are mutually exclusive.

parameters.name: authorization_services_enabled
parameters.description: Are authorization services enabled for this client or not (OpenID connect). This is authorizationServicesEnabled in the Keycloak REST API. Choices: false true

parameters.name: authorization_settings
parameters.description: A data structure defining the authorization settings for this client. For reference, please see the Keycloak API docs at https://www.keycloak.org/docs-api/8.0/rest-api/index.html#_resourceserverrepresentation. This is authorizationSettings in the Keycloak REST API.

parameters.name: backchannel_logout_url
parameters.description: URL that will cause the client to log itself out when a logout request is sent to this realm. This is stored as backchannel.logout.url in the client attributes.

parameters.name: base_url
parameters.description: Default URL to use when the auth server needs to redirect or link back to the client This is baseUrl in the Keycloak REST API.

parameters.name: bearer_only
parameters.description: The access type of this client is bearer-only. This is bearerOnly in the Keycloak REST API. Choices: false true

parameters.name: client_authenticator_type
parameters.description: How do clients authenticate with the auth server? Either client-secret, client-jwt, or client-x509 can be chosen. When using client-secret, the module parameter secret can set it, for client-jwt, you can use the keys use.jwks.url, jwks.url, and jwt.credential.certificate in the attributes module parameter to configure its behavior. For client-x509 you can use the keys x509.allow.regex.pattern.comparison and x509.subjectdn in the attributes module parameter to configure which certificate(s) to accept. This is clientAuthenticatorType in the Keycloak REST API. Choices: "client-secret" "client-jwt" "client-x509"

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: Client ID of client to be worked on. This is usually an alphanumeric name chosen by you. Either this or id is required. If you specify both, id takes precedence. This is clientId in the Keycloak REST API.

parameters.name: client_scopes_behavior
parameters.description: Determine how default_client_scopes and optional_client_scopes behave when updating an existing client. ignore: Do not change the client scopes of an existing client. This is the default for backward compatibility. patch: Add missing scopes, do not remove any missing scopes. idempotent: Make the client scopes exactly as specified, adding and removing scopes as needed. Choices: "ignore" ← (default) "patch" "idempotent"

parameters.name: client_template
parameters.description: Client template to use for this client. If it does not exist this field is silently dropped. This is clientTemplate in the Keycloak REST API.

parameters.name: connection_timeout
parameters.description: Controls the HTTP connections timeout period (in seconds) to Keycloak API. Default: 10

parameters.name: consent_required
parameters.description: If enabled, users have to consent to client access. This is consentRequired in the Keycloak REST API. Choices: false true

parameters.name: default_client_scopes
parameters.description: List of default client scopes. See client_scopes_behavior for how this behaves when updating an existing client.

parameters.name: default_roles
parameters.description: List of default roles for this client. If the client roles referenced do not exist yet, they are created. This is defaultRoles in the Keycloak REST API.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Description of the client in Keycloak.

parameters.name: direct_access_grants_enabled
parameters.description: Are direct access grants enabled for this client or not (OpenID connect). This is directAccessGrantsEnabled in the Keycloak REST API. Choices: false true

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: Is this client enabled or not? Choices: false true

parameters.name: frontchannel_logout
parameters.description: Is frontchannel logout enabled for this client or not. This is frontchannelLogout in the Keycloak REST API. Choices: false true

parameters.name: full_scope_allowed
parameters.description: Is the “Full Scope Allowed” feature set for this client or not. This is fullScopeAllowed in the Keycloak REST API. Choices: false true

parameters.name: http_agent
parameters.description: Configures the HTTP User-Agent header. Default: "Ansible"

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of client to be worked on. This is usually an UUID. Either this or client_id is required. If you specify both, this takes precedence.

parameters.name: implicit_flow_enabled
parameters.description: Enable implicit flow for this client or not (OpenID connect). This is implicitFlowEnabled in the Keycloak REST API. Choices: false true

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name of the client (this is not the same as client_id).

parameters.name: node_re_registration_timeout
parameters.description: Cluster node re-registration timeout for this client. This is nodeReRegistrationTimeout in the Keycloak REST API.

parameters.name: not_before
parameters.description: Revoke any tokens issued before this date for this client (this is a UNIX timestamp). This is notBefore in the Keycloak REST API.

parameters.name: optional_client_scopes
parameters.description: List of optional client scopes. See client_scopes_behavior for how this behaves when updating an existing client.

parameters.name: protocol
parameters.description: Type of client. At creation only, default value is openid-connect if protocol is omitted. The docker-v2 value was added in community.general 8.6.0. Choices: "openid-connect" "saml" "docker-v2"

parameters.name: protocol_mappers
parameters.description: A list of dicts defining protocol mappers for this client. This is protocolMappers in the Keycloak REST API.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: Dict specifying the configuration options for the protocol mapper; the contents differ depending on the value of protocol_mappers[].protocolMapper and are not documented other than by the source of the mappers and its parent class(es). An example is given below. It is easiest to obtain valid config values by dumping an already-existing protocol mapper configuration through check-mode in the existing field.

parameters.name: consentRequired
parameters.description: Specifies whether a user needs to provide consent to a client for this mapper to be active. Choices: false true

parameters.name: consentText
parameters.description: The human-readable name of the consent the user is presented to accept.

parameters.name: protocolMapper
parameters.description: The Keycloak-internal name of the type of this protocol-mapper. While an exhaustive list is impossible to provide since this may be extended through SPIs by the user of Keycloak, by default Keycloak as of 3.4 ships with at least: docker-v2-allow-all-mapper. oidc-address-mapper. oidc-full-name-mapper. oidc-group-membership-mapper. oidc-hardcoded-claim-mapper. oidc-hardcoded-role-mapper. oidc-role-name-mapper. oidc-script-based-protocol-mapper. oidc-sha256-pairwise-sub-mapper. oidc-usermodel-attribute-mapper. oidc-usermodel-client-role-mapper. oidc-usermodel-property-mapper. oidc-usermodel-realm-role-mapper. oidc-usersessionmodel-note-mapper. saml-group-membership-mapper. saml-hardcode-attribute-mapper. saml-hardcode-role-mapper. saml-role-list-mapper. saml-role-name-mapper. saml-user-attribute-mapper. saml-user-property-mapper. saml-user-session-note-mapper. An exhaustive list of available mappers on your installation can be obtained on the admin console by going to Server Info -> Providers and looking under ‘protocol-mapper’.

parameters.name: public_client
parameters.description: Is the access type for this client public or not. This is publicClient in the Keycloak REST API. Choices: false true

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: The realm to create the client in. Default: "master"

parameters.name: redirect_uris
parameters.description: Acceptable redirect URIs for this client. This is redirectUris in the Keycloak REST API.

parameters.name: refresh_token
parameters.description: Authentication refresh token for Keycloak API.

parameters.name: registered_nodes
parameters.description: Dict of registered cluster nodes (with nodename as the key and last registration time as the value). This is registeredNodes in the Keycloak REST API.

parameters.name: registration_access_token
parameters.description: The registration access token provides access for clients to the client registration service. This is registrationAccessToken in the Keycloak REST API.

parameters.name: root_url
parameters.description: Root URL appended to relative URLs for this client. This is rootUrl in the Keycloak REST API.

parameters.name: secret
parameters.description: When using client_authenticator_type=client-secret (the default), you can specify a secret here (otherwise one is generated if it does not exit). If changing this secret, the module does not register a change currently (but the changed secret is saved).

parameters.name: service_accounts_enabled
parameters.description: Are service accounts enabled for this client or not (OpenID connect). This is serviceAccountsEnabled in the Keycloak REST API. Choices: false true

parameters.name: standard_flow_enabled
parameters.description: Enable standard flow for this client or not (OpenID connect). This is standardFlowEnabled in the Keycloak REST API. Choices: false true

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: State of the client. On present, the client are created (or updated if it exists already). On absent, the client are removed if it exists. Choices: "present" ← (default) "absent"

parameters.name: surrogate_auth_required
parameters.description: Whether or not surrogate auth is required. This is surrogateAuthRequired in the Keycloak REST API. Choices: false true

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Authentication token for Keycloak API.

parameters.name: use_template_config
parameters.description: Whether or not to use configuration from the client_template. This is useTemplateConfig in the Keycloak REST API. Choices: false true

parameters.name: use_template_mappers
parameters.description: Whether or not to use mapper configuration from the client_template. This is useTemplateMappers in the Keycloak REST API. Choices: false true

parameters.name: use_template_scope
parameters.description: Whether or not to use scope configuration from the client_template. This is useTemplateScope in the Keycloak REST API. Choices: false true

parameters.name: valid_post_logout_redirect_uris
parameters.description: Valid post logout redirect URIs for this client. This is stored as post.logout.redirect.uris in the client attributes. Use + as a single list element to allow all redirect URIs.

parameters.name: validate_certs
parameters.description: Verify TLS certificates (do not disable this in production). Choices: false true ← (default)

parameters.name: web_origins
parameters.description: List of allowed CORS origins. This is webOrigins in the Keycloak REST API.

examples:
- name: Create or update Keycloak client (minimal example), authentication with credentials
  community.general.keycloak_client:
    auth_keycloak_url: https://auth.example.com/auth
    auth_realm: master
    auth_username: USERNAME
    auth_password: PASSWORD
    client_id: test
    state: present
  delegate_to: localhost


- name: Create or update Keycloak client (minimal example), authentication with token
  community.general.keycloak_client:
    auth_client_id: admin-cli
    auth_keycloak_url: https://auth.example.com/auth
    auth_realm: master
    token: TOKEN
    client_id: test
    state: present
  delegate_to: localhost


- name: Delete a Keycloak client
  community.general.keycloak_client:
    auth_client_id: admin-cli
    auth_keycloak_url: https://auth.example.com/auth
    auth_realm: master
    auth_username: USERNAME
    auth_password: PASSWORD
    client_id: test
    state: absent
  delegate_to: localhost


- name: Create or update a Keycloak client (minimal example), with x509 authentication
  community.general.keycloak_client:
    auth_client_id: admin-cli
    auth_keycloak_url: https://auth.example.com/auth
    auth_realm: master
    auth_username: USERNAME
    auth_password: PASSWORD
    realm: master
    state: present
    client_id: test
    client_authenticator_type: client-x509
    attributes:
      x509.subjectdn: "CN=client"
      x509.allow.regex.pattern.comparison: false


- name: Create or update a Keycloak client (with all the bells and whistles)
  community.general.keycloak_client:
    auth_client_id: admin-cli
    auth_keycloak_url: https://auth.example.com/auth
    auth_realm: master
    auth_username: USERNAME
    auth_password: PASSWORD
    state: present
    realm: master
    client_id: test
    id: d8b127a3-31f6-44c8-a7e4-4ab9a3e78d95
    name: this_is_a_test
    description: Description of this wonderful client
    root_url: https://www.example.com/
    admin_url: https://www.example.com/admin_url
    base_url: basepath
    enabled: true
    client_authenticator_type: client-secret
    secret: REALLYWELLKEPTSECRET
    redirect_uris:
      - https://www.example.com/*
      - http://localhost:8888/
    web_origins:
      - https://www.example.com/*
    not_before: 1507825725
    bearer_only: false
    consent_required: false
    standard_flow_enabled: true
    implicit_flow_enabled: false
    direct_access_grants_enabled: false
    service_accounts_enabled: false
    authorization_services_enabled: false
    public_client: false
    frontchannel_logout: false
    protocol: openid-connect
    full_scope_allowed: false
    node_re_registration_timeout: -1
    client_template: test
    use_template_config: false
    use_template_scope: false
    use_template_mappers: false
    always_display_in_console: true
    registered_nodes:
      node01.example.com: 1507828202
    registration_access_token: eyJWT_TOKEN
    surrogate_auth_required: false
    default_roles:
      - test01
      - test02
    authentication_flow_binding_overrides:
      browser: 4c90336b-bf1d-4b87-916d-3677ba4e5fbb
    protocol_mappers:
      - config:
          access.token.claim: true
          claim.name: "family_name"
          id.token.claim: true
          jsonType.label: String
          user.attribute: lastName
          userinfo.token.claim: true
        consentRequired: true
        consentText: "${familyName}"
        name: family name
        protocol: openid-connect
        protocolMapper: oidc-usermodel-property-mapper
      - config:
          attribute.name: Role
          attribute.nameformat: Basic
          single: false
        consentRequired: false
        name: role list
        protocol: saml
        protocolMapper: saml-role-list-mapper
    attributes:
      saml.authnstatement: true
      saml.client.signature: true
      saml.force.post.binding: true
      saml.server.signature: true
      saml.signature.algorithm: RSA_SHA256
      saml.signing.certificate: CERTIFICATEHERE
      saml.signing.private.key: PRIVATEKEYHERE
      saml_force_name_id_format: false
      saml_name_id_format: username
      saml_signature_canonicalization_method: "http://www.w3.org/2001/10/xml-exc-c14n#"
      user.info.response.signature.alg: RS256
      request.object.signature.alg: RS256
      use.jwks.url: true
      jwks.url: JWKS_URL_FOR_CLIENT_AUTH_JWT
      jwt.credential.certificate: JWT_CREDENTIAL_CERTIFICATE_FOR_CLIENT_AUTH
  delegate_to: localhost

return_values.name: end_state
return_values.description: Representation of client after module execution (sample is truncated). Returned: on success Sample: {"adminUrl": "http://www.example.com/admin_url", "attributes": {"request.object.signature.alg": "RS256"}}

return_values.name: existing
return_values.description: Representation of existing client (sample is truncated). Returned: always Sample: {"adminUrl": "http://www.example.com/admin_url", "attributes": {"request.object.signature.alg": "RS256"}}

return_values.name: msg
return_values.description: Message as to what action was taken. Returned: always Sample: "Client testclient has been updated"

return_values.name: proposed
return_values.description: Representation of proposed client. Returned: always Sample: {"clientId": "test"}
